title: Identifying Code Smells in Shape Processing
question: Review the C++ code snippet below. Which code smell is most prominently exhibited in this Shape processing system?
explanation: The code exhibits a classic 'Switch Statements' smell. The same enum-based switch structure is repeated in multiple places (calculateArea, calculatePerimeter, draw, renderShape, exportToSVG), all switching on the same ShapeType enum. Each time a new shape is added, every switch statement would need to be updated, leading to scattered changes throughout the codebase. This violates the Open-Closed Principle, as the code isn't open for extension without requiring modification. The proper refactoring would be to use polymorphism by creating a base Shape class with virtual methods, and implementing concrete subclasses for each shape type. This way, adding a new shape only requires adding a new class without modifying existing code.
